'''Krishna Lynne Foster''' (born January 7, 1970) is an American environmental chemist who is a professor at [[California State University, Los Angeles]]. Her research considers the impact of sunlight on pollutants. Foster has worked to improve the representation of people of colour studying chemistry.

== Early life and education ==
Foster was born in [[Culver City, California]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Krishna Foster's Biography|url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/krishna-foster-42|access-date=2020-08-02|website=The HistoryMakers|language=en}}</ref> Her parents, Warren and Frances Foster, worked at [[IBM]] and [[San Diego State University]].<ref name=":0" /> Foster has said that he was always encouraged to work hard, and she eventually attended the [[Helix High School]].<ref name=":0" /> She has said that she enjoyed baking as a child, primarily because of how much chemistry it involved.<ref name=":0" /> Whilst still a teenager, Foster was awarded a [[NASA]] women in science fellowship. Foster attended [[Spelman College]], which she graduated in 1992.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Krishna Foster, C'92|url=https://www.spelman.edu/about-us/news-and-events/our-stories/stories/2015/09/12/krishna-foster-c-92|access-date=2020-08-21|website=www.spelman.edu}}</ref> As a student at Spelman, Foster took classes in environmental chemistry, and decided that this was a research area she would like to pursue. She moved to the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] for her graduate studies, where she specialised in [[hydrogen halide]]s. In 1998 she moved back to [[California]], joining [[University of California, Irvine]] as a postdoctoral researcher, where she worked alongside [[Barbara J. Finlayson-Pitts]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last1=Foster|first1=Krishna|date=2002-03-01|title=Awakening at Sunrise: How My Arctic Experience Shaped My Career Goals|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/awakening-sunrise-how-my-arctic-experience-shaped-my-career-goals|access-date=2020-08-02|website=Science {{!}} AAAS|language=en}}</ref> Here her work made use of [[mass spectrometry]] to investigate sea salt particles.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
Foster was appointed to the faculty at [[California State University, Los Angeles]] in 2000. That year she took part in Alert 2000, an international fieldwork programme to study the photochemistry of snow in [[Alert, Nunavut]].<ref name=":1" /> Her research proposal looked to measure the concentrations of gaseous halogens using [[atmospheric-pressure chemical ionization]].<ref name=":1" /> She has said that she joined Cal State LA because it valued teaching as much as research.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Krishna Foster, Ph.D. {{!}} CSU|url=https://www2.calstate.edu:443/impact-of-the-csu/student-success/Profiles/Pages/krishna-foster.aspx|access-date=2020-08-02|website=www2.calstate.edu|language=en-US}}</ref> There she has studied the impact of sunlight on pollutants, primarily at the air/water interface. She was awarded tenure in 2006 and the California State University, Los Angeles Distinguished Women Award in 2007.<ref name=":0" /> Beyond her work on pollutants, Foster has studied how [[phosphorus]] might have first been incorporated into living cells.

Foster has worked to make science and technology more inclusive and more welcoming to students of colour.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Biography Page for Krishna Foster|url=http://www.idvl.org/sciencemakers/Bio37.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151107215228/http://www.idvl.org/sciencemakers/Bio37.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=November 7, 2015|access-date=2020-08-02|website=www.idvl.org}}</ref> She established the Cal State Minorities Opportunities in Research programme, which introduces students from marginalised backgrounds to research methods. The [[National Science Foundation]] named Cal State LA as one of the top institutions for [[Latin Americans]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=2016-08-25|title=Cal State LA professor recognized as Minority Access National Role Model|url=http://www.calstatela.edu/univ/ppa/publicat/cal-state-la-professor-recognized-minority-access-national-role-model|access-date=2020-08-02|website=Cal State LA|language=en}}</ref> She made use of the [[American Chemical Society]] Project SEED initiative to host Black chemists in her research lab.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2014–15 Project SEED College Scholarships|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/93/i11/201415-Project-SEED-College-Scholarships.html|access-date=2020-08-02|website=Chemical & Engineering News|language=en}}</ref> For her efforts, she was named a Minority Access National Role Model.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-09-01|title=Cal State LA chemistry professor recognized as Minority Access National Role Model|url=https://lasentinel.net/cal-state-la-chemistry-professor-recognized-as-minority-access-national-role-model.html|access-date=2020-08-02|website=Los Angeles Sentinel|language=en-US}}</ref> She is the Director of the Minority Biomedical Research Support-Research Initiative for Scientific Enhancement) (MBBRS-RISE) programme, which supports students of colour who look to become research scientists.
